name: IRS/Census — EITC participation rates (State, TY2014-2022; national CPS series, TY2019-2022)
organization: Internal Revenue Service with the U.S. Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies
citation: Coleman, Ciyata, Charles Hokayem, Sanghun (Eric) Kim, Ethan Krohn, Krishnan Patel and Dean Plueger. "EITC Participation Results and IRS-Census Match Methodology, Tax Year 2021." U.S. Census Bureau CES Working Paper 24-75, December 2024. (The same file is posted at irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/24rpeitcunderclaimsty2021census.pdf.)
published: State table: undated web page, TY2022 edition current as fetched 2026-10-06; CES-WP-24-75: 2024-12

model.name: IRS-Census Exact Match (survey records linked to IRS returns)
model.method: Participation = eligible taxpayers receiving an EITC payment / taxpayers eligible for the EITC. Eligibility is modeled from survey income and demographic data (ACS for the State table, CPS ASEC for the national headline), including non-filers; receipt comes from IRS records. Taxpayers and tax units are used interchangeably.
model.method_basis: IRS page footnotes 1-2; CES-WP-24-75 methodology section

period: State table: tax years 2014-2022 (ACS). National CPS series: tax years 2019-2021 (CES-WP-24-75 Tables 1-3) and tax year 2022 (IRS page footnote 2).
geographies: 50 States, DC and national (State table); national only (CPS series)
coverage_note: No State-level eligible counts or by-children rates are published with the State table; the CES paper's by-children and by-filing-status rates are stated in prose only and are not extracted.
vintage_note: Tax year 2021 is the ARPA year (childless EITC expanded for that year only), so CPS TY2021 eligibility is not comparable with other years. The State table's older editions (TY2013-2020, May 2024) match the current edition cell for cell where they overlap.
diagnosis_upstream: The IRS-Census model is not public; divergences classified as external-model issues become a comparison memo, not an upstream PR.
